ledger.note: 5600 BCE: the Cardial leaps west from Liguria to Portugal and Morocco. "2,000 km from the gulf of Genoa to the estuary of the Mondego in probably no more than 100-200 years"; "all secure radiocarbon dates are identical to those for Iberia c. 5500 cal BC"; the earliest North-West African Neolithic remains "c. 5400 BC". [Reviewer xx-01-a, 2026-10-18: confidence 2 to 1: the page gives no date for the western arc (Iberia "c. 5500 cal BC"); 5600 is the dossier's placement, as the keyframe note says. Tangier (60 km) removed: the page dates the north-west African Neolithic "c. 5400 BC", after this dossier's 5500 BCE end]

Infobox end "c. 5500 BC"; "Followed by: Danilo culture, Kakanj culture, Stentinello culture, Neolithic Italy, Neolithic Malta, Neolithic Sardinia, Neolithic France, Neolithic Iberia, La Hoguette culture", none with a dossier; the "epi-Cardial" styles continue locally.

sources.title: Cardium pottery
sources.note: Dates 6400-5500 BC, the spread from Epirus to the Adriatic, Italy, Sardinia, Provence, Iberia and Morocco with its radiocarbon dates, the successor cultures.

notes: Culture dossier, one page. The dissolve at 5500 BCE follows the infobox although the western Cardial had only just arrived: the Western Mediterranean Neolithic after 5500 BCE (Epicardial, Danilo, Stentinello, Chasséen, the Iberian Neolithic) has no dossier and is nobody's land until the Atlantic megalith builders (4800 BCE) and, much later, the first states (gap). Andalusia, Corsica and Malta are not on the page. Gazetteer: Coppa Nevigata, Su Carroppu are not places; regions and radii stand in.
